source.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ שִׁמְשׁ֖וֹן עַזָּ֑תָה וַיַּרְא־שָׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה זוֹנָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א אֵלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Samson to Gaza, and he saw there a woman, a prostitute, and he went in to her.

en.L: And Samson went to Gaza, and he saw there a woman, a prostitute, and he went in to her.
en.B: Samson went to Gaza. There he saw a prostitute, and he went in and slept with her.
en.R: One day Samson went to Gaza, a Philistine city. There he saw a prostitute, and he slept with her.

sw.L: Naye Samsoni akaenda Gaza, akamwona huko mwanamke kahaba, akaingia kwake.
sw.B: Samsoni alikwenda Gaza. Huko alimwona kahaba mmoja, akaingia kwake akalala naye.
sw.R: Siku moja Samsoni alikwenda Gaza, mji wa Wafilisti. Huko alimwona kahaba mmoja, akalala naye.

es.L: Y fue Sansón a Gaza, y vio allí a una mujer, una prostituta, y entró a ella.
es.B: Sansón fue a Gaza. Allí vio a una prostituta y entró a acostarse con ella.
es.R: Un día Sansón fue a Gaza, una ciudad filistea. Allí vio a una prostituta y se acostó con ella.

decisions.choice: Gaza: a Philistine city on the coast
decisions.reason: Gaza was the southernmost of the five Philistine cities (Joshua 13:3), near the sea, far from Samson's home in Zorah. He walks alone into the heart of enemy land.

decisions.choice: a woman who was a prostitute
decisions.reason: As at Joshua 2:1, the word (zonah) is the ordinary word for a woman who sells sex. The story does not soften it.

decisions.choice: he went in to her: he had sex with her
decisions.reason: "Go in to" a woman is a plain way of saying a man had sex with her (Genesis 16:4; 38:18). The chapter opens as Samson's story has run so far: he goes after what he sees (14:1-3).

decisions.choice: slept with her; Readable "a Philistine city"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "went in to her" means (m3). Readable also says what Gaza was (m1).

source.text: לַֽעַזָּתִ֣ים׀לֵאמֹ֗ר בָּ֤א שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ הֵ֔נָּה וַיָּסֹ֛בּוּ וַיֶּאֶרְבוּ־ל֥וֹ כָל־הַלַּ֖יְלָה בְּשַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֑יר וַיִּתְחָרְשׁ֤וּ כָל־הַלַּ֨יְלָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר עַד־א֥וֹר הַבֹּ֖קֶר וַהֲרְגְנֻֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: To the Gazites, saying, has come Samson here. And they surrounded and lay in wait for him all the night at [the] gate of the city, and they kept quiet all the night, saying, until [the] light of the morning, and we will kill him.

en.L: [It was told] to the Gazites, "Samson has come here." And they surrounded [the place] and lay in wait for him all night at the gate of the city. And they kept quiet all night, saying, "Until the light of the morning; then we will kill him."
en.B: The people of Gaza were told, "Samson has come here!" So they surrounded the place and lay in ambush for him at the city gate through the night. They made no move the whole night, for they said, "When morning light comes, we will kill him."
en.R: Someone told the people of Gaza, "Samson is here!" So they surrounded the place. All night long they hid and waited for him at the city gate. They kept still the whole night. They said, "When it gets light in the morning, we will kill him."

sw.L: [Ikaambiwa] kwa Wagaza, "Samsoni amekuja hapa." Nao wakazunguka [mahali hapo], wakamvizia usiku wote kwenye lango la mji. Nao wakanyamaza usiku wote, wakisema, "Mpaka mwanga wa asubuhi; ndipo tutamwua."
sw.B: Watu wa Gaza waliambiwa, "Samsoni amekuja hapa!" Basi walipazunguka mahali pale, wakamvizia usiku kucha kwenye lango la mji. Hawakufanya lolote usiku wote, kwa maana walisema, "Mwanga wa asubuhi utakapokuja, tutamwua."
sw.R: Mtu mmoja aliwaambia watu wa Gaza, "Samsoni yuko hapa!" Kwa hiyo walipazunguka mahali pale. Usiku kucha walijificha wakimngoja kwenye lango la mji. Walikaa kimya usiku wote. Walisema, "Kutakapokucha asubuhi, tutamwua."

es.L: [Se dijo] a los de Gaza: «Sansón ha venido aquí». Y [lo] rodearon y le pusieron emboscada toda la noche a la puerta de la ciudad. Y estuvieron callados toda la noche, diciendo: «Hasta la luz de la mañana; entonces lo mataremos».
es.B: A la gente de Gaza le avisaron: «¡Sansón ha venido aquí!». Así que rodearon el lugar y estuvieron toda la noche al acecho junto a la puerta de la ciudad. No se movieron en toda la noche, porque se decían: «Cuando llegue la luz de la mañana, lo mataremos».
es.R: Alguien les avisó a los de Gaza: «¡Sansón está aquí!». Entonces rodearon el lugar. Toda la noche estuvieron escondidos esperándolo junto a la puerta de la ciudad. Se quedaron quietos toda la noche. Decían: «Cuando amanezca, lo mataremos».

decisions.choice: [It was told] to the Gazites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence has no verb: it says only "To the Gazites, saying". The ancient Greek translation reads "and it was told to the Gazites", which may keep a word lost from the Hebrew, or may simply supply what the sense needs. Either way the meaning is the same: someone brought word that Samson was in the city. This description comes from general knowledge of the Greek and should be checked against its manuscripts.

decisions.choice: they kept quiet all night: they waited for dawn
decisions.reason: The men did nothing during the night. The city gate was shut at night, so they expected to catch Samson when it opened in the morning and he tried to leave.

decisions.choice: the gate of the city
decisions.reason: A walled city had one main gate, closed and barred at night (Joshua 2:5, 7). Anyone leaving had to pass through it, so it was the place for an ambush.

decisions.choice: [It was told] (L); were told / Someone told (B, R); [the place] (L)
decisions.reason: The verb the sense needs is supplied (m1), and so is the object of "surrounded", which the Hebrew leaves out.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב שִׁמְשׁוֹן֮ עַד־חֲצִ֣י הַלַּיְלָה֒ וַיָּ֣קָם׀בַּחֲצִ֣י הַלַּ֗יְלָה וַיֶּאֱחֹ֞ז בְּדַלְת֤וֹת שַֽׁעַר־הָעִיר֙ וּבִשְׁתֵּ֣י הַמְּזוּז֔וֹת וַיִּסָּעֵם֙ עִֽם־הַבְּרִ֔יחַ וַיָּ֖שֶׂם עַל־כְּתֵפָ֑יו וַֽיַּעֲלֵם֙ אֶל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י חֶבְרֽוֹן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And lay Samson until [the] middle of the night, and he arose in [the] middle of the night and took hold of [the] doors of [the] gate of the city and of [the] two posts and pulled them up with the bar, and put [them] on his shoulders and carried them up to [the] top of the hill that [is] before Hebron.

en.L: And Samson lay until the middle of the night, and he arose at the middle of the night and took hold of the doors of the gate of the city and of the two doorposts, and pulled them up with the bar, and put [them] on his shoulders and carried them up to the top of the hill that [is] in front of Hebron.
en.B: But Samson lay there only until midnight. At midnight he got up and seized the doors of the city gate together with its two posts, and he tore them loose, bar and all. Lifting them onto his shoulders, he carried them all the way up to the hilltop that faces Hebron.
en.R: But Samson stayed in bed only until midnight. Then he got up and went to the city gate. He grabbed its two doors and the two posts beside them. He pulled the whole gate out of the ground, with the bar that locked it. He put it all on his shoulders. Then he carried it up to the top of the hill that looks toward Hebron.

sw.L: Naye Samsoni akalala mpaka usiku wa manane, akaondoka usiku wa manane, akaishika milango ya lango la mji na miimo yake miwili, akaing'oa pamoja na komeo, akaiweka mabegani mwake, akaipandisha mpaka kilele cha kilima kilichoko mbele ya Hebroni.
sw.B: Lakini Samsoni alilala huko mpaka usiku wa manane tu. Usiku wa manane aliamka, akaishika milango ya lango la mji pamoja na miimo yake miwili, akaing'oa yote pamoja na komeo lake. Akaiweka mabegani mwake, akaipandisha mpaka juu ya kilima kinachoelekea Hebroni.
sw.R: Lakini Samsoni alikaa kitandani mpaka usiku wa manane tu. Kisha aliamka, akaenda kwenye lango la mji. Aliishika milango yake miwili na nguzo mbili zilizokuwa kando yake. Aling'oa lango lote ardhini, pamoja na komeo lililolifunga. Aliliweka lote mabegani mwake. Kisha akalibeba mpaka juu ya kilima kinachotazama Hebroni.

es.L: Y Sansón estuvo acostado hasta la medianoche, y a la medianoche se levantó y agarró las puertas de la entrada de la ciudad y los dos postes, y las arrancó junto con la tranca, y [las] puso sobre sus hombros y las subió a la cumbre del monte que [está] frente a Hebrón.
es.B: Pero Sansón se quedó acostado solo hasta la medianoche. A medianoche se levantó, agarró las puertas de la entrada de la ciudad junto con sus dos postes y las arrancó con tranca y todo. Se las echó al hombro y las subió hasta la cumbre del monte que está frente a Hebrón.
es.R: Pero Sansón se quedó en la cama solo hasta la medianoche. Entonces se levantó y fue a la entrada de la ciudad. Agarró sus dos puertas y los dos postes que estaban a los lados. Arrancó toda la entrada del suelo, con la tranca que la cerraba. Se lo echó todo al hombro y lo llevó hasta la cumbre del monte que mira hacia Hebrón.

decisions.choice: the doors, the doorposts and the bar: the whole gate
decisions.reason: The bar was the beam laid across the closed doors to lock them. Samson tears out doors, posts and bar together. A city without its gate lay open to any enemy, and its people were put to shame.

decisions.choice: the hill in front of Hebron
alternatives: a hill near Gaza from which one looks toward Hebron
decisions.reason: Hebron lies in the hill country of Judah, about 40 miles from Gaza and some 3,000 feet higher. "In front of Hebron" may mean a hill near Hebron, or a hill on the way that faces toward it. Either way the gate of the Philistine city ends up on a hill in Israel's land.

decisions.choice: Samson lay until midnight
decisions.reason: The verb picks up verse 1: he stayed with the woman. Leaving at midnight, he escaped the men who were waiting for morning (verse 2).

decisions.choice: pulled the whole gate out of the ground, with the bar that locked it
decisions.reason: Readable says what the bar was for and that the posts came out of the ground with the doors (m1).

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֔ן וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב אִשָּׁ֖ה בְּנַ֣חַל שֹׂרֵ֑ק וּשְׁמָ֖הּ דְּלִילָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after thus, and he loved a woman in [the] valley of Sorek, and her name [was] Delilah.

en.L: And it came about after this that he loved a woman in the Valley of Sorek, and her name [was] Delilah.
en.B: Some time after this, he fell in love with a woman named Delilah, in the Valley of Sorek.
en.R: Later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah. She lived in the Valley of Sorek.

sw.L: Ikawa baada ya hayo akampenda mwanamke katika bonde la Soreki, na jina lake [lilikuwa] Delila.
sw.B: Baada ya muda alimpenda mwanamke mmoja aitwaye Delila, katika bonde la Soreki.
sw.R: Baadaye Samsoni alimpenda mwanamke mmoja aitwaye Delila. Aliishi katika bonde la Soreki.

es.L: Y sucedió después de esto que amó a una mujer en el valle de Sorec, y su nombre [era] Dalila.
es.B: Algún tiempo después, se enamoró de una mujer llamada Dalila, del valle de Sorec.
es.R: Más tarde, Sansón se enamoró de una mujer llamada Dalila. Ella vivía en el valle de Sorec.

decisions.choice: the Valley of Sorek
decisions.reason: The valley runs west from the hills near Zorah and Eshtaol, Samson's home, down toward Philistine land; Timnah lay near it (14:1). It was border country between Israel and the Philistines. The name probably comes from a word for choice red grapes (Isaiah 5:2).

decisions.choice: Delilah: her people are not named
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether Delilah was a Philistine or an Israelite, or that Samson married her. The Philistine rulers come to her as someone they can buy (verse 5). The meaning of her name is not certain.

decisions.choice: he loved a woman
decisions.reason: This is the first time the text says Samson loved a woman. It never says that Delilah loved him.

decisions.choice: fell in love with
decisions.reason: The verb describes the start of his love here, so Balanced and Readable say "fell in love"; Literal keeps "loved".

decisions.choice: "Dalila", "el valle de Sorec", "Gaza", "Dagón"
decisions.reason: The names in their usual Spanish forms, as the terms note sets for Delilah.

source.text: וַיַּעֲל֨וּ אֵלֶ֜יהָ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיֹּ֨אמְרוּ לָ֜הּ פַּתִּ֣י אוֹת֗וֹ וּרְאִי֙ בַּמֶּה֙ כֹּח֣וֹ גָד֔וֹל וּבַמֶּה֙ נ֣וּכַל ל֔וֹ וַאֲסַרְנֻ֖הוּ לְעַנֹּת֑וֹ וַאֲנַ֨חְנוּ֙ נִתַּן־לָ֔ךְ אִ֕ישׁ אֶ֥לֶף וּמֵאָ֖ה כָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And came up to her [the] rulers of [the] Philistines and said to her, entice him and see in what his strength [is] great and by what we will prevail over him, and we will bind him to humble him; and we, we will give you each a thousand and a hundred silver.

en.L: And the rulers of the Philistines came up to her and said to her, "Entice him, and see in what his great strength [lies], and by what we may overpower him, so that we may bind him to subdue him. And we will each give you 1,100 [shekels of] silver."
en.B: The rulers of the Philistines came up to her and said, "Coax him, and find out what makes his strength so great and how we can overpower him, so that we can tie him up and subdue him. Each of us will give you {{units:about 28 pounds of silver|1,100 shekels of silver}}."
en.R: The rulers of the Philistines came to see her. They said, "Trick Samson into telling you his secret. Find out what makes him so strong. Find out how we can overpower him, so we can tie him up and make him helpless. If you do, each of us will pay you {{units:about 28 pounds of silver|1,100 shekels of silver}}."

sw.L: Nao watawala wa Wafilisti wakapanda kwake, wakamwambia, "Mshawishi, uone nguvu zake nyingi [ziko] katika nini, na kwa nini tutaweza kumshinda, ili tumfunge kumtiisha. Nasi kila mmoja wetu atakupa [shekeli] 1,100 za fedha."
sw.B: Watawala wa Wafilisti walipanda kwake, wakamwambia, "Mbembeleze, ujue ni nini kinachompa nguvu nyingi hivyo, na jinsi tunavyoweza kumshinda, ili tumfunge na kumtiisha. Kila mmoja wetu atakupa {{units:karibu kilo 13 za fedha|shekeli 1,100 za fedha}}."
sw.R: Watawala wa Wafilisti walikuja kumwona. Walisema, "Mdanganye Samsoni akuambie siri yake. Tafuta ni nini kinachompa nguvu nyingi hivyo. Tafuta jinsi tunavyoweza kumshinda, ili tumfunge na kumfanya asiweze kufanya lolote. Ukifanya hivyo, kila mmoja wetu atakulipa {{units:karibu kilo 13 za fedha|shekeli 1,100 za fedha}}."

es.L: Y subieron a ella los jefes de los filisteos y le dijeron: «Sedúcelo y mira en qué [está] su gran fuerza y con qué podremos vencerlo, para que lo atemos para someterlo. Y nosotros te daremos cada uno 1100 [siclos de] plata».
es.B: Los jefes de los filisteos subieron a verla y le dijeron: «Sedúcelo y averigua de dónde le viene esa fuerza tan grande y cómo podremos vencerlo, para atarlo y someterlo. Cada uno de nosotros te dará {{units:unos 13 kilos de plata|1100 siclos de plata}}».
es.R: Los jefes de los filisteos fueron a verla. Le dijeron: «Engaña a Sansón para que te diga su secreto. Averigua por qué es tan fuerte. Averigua cómo podemos vencerlo, para atarlo y dejarlo indefenso. Si lo haces, cada uno de nosotros te pagará {{units:unos 13 kilos de plata|1100 siclos de plata}}».

decisions.choice: the rulers of the Philistines
decisions.reason: The word (seren) is used only of the rulers of the five Philistine cities (Joshua 13:3; Judges 3:3) and may be a Philistine word. All five come together to deal with Samson.

decisions.choice: entice him: coax him into telling
decisions.reason: The verb means to persuade someone by charm or trickery. The Philistines said the same to Samson's wife at Timnah (14:15).

decisions.choice: to subdue him
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring someone low: to overpower him, and also to humiliate or mistreat him. It returns in verses 6 and 19.

decisions.choice: 1,100 pieces of silver from each ruler
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "1,100 silver"; the unit is the shekel, a weight. From five rulers that makes 5,500 shekels, a huge sum: a priest's yearly pay was ten shekels (17:10).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 28 pounds of silver|1,100 shekels of silver}}
decisions.reason: About 2/5 ounce to the shekel gives about 440 ounces, about 28 pounds. The units setting gives the original "1,100 shekels". Literal keeps the Hebrew count and brackets the unit it leaves out.

decisions.choice: Trick Samson into telling you his secret ... If you do
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "entice him" aims at (m2) and makes the condition of the payment plain.

decisions.choice: metric weight by default ("karibu kilo 13"), with "1,100 shekels" as the reader setting; Literal keeps the shekels
alternatives: US pounds as in the English
decisions.reason: As the Swahili style guide sets for measures: metric by default, at the shekel value of 11.5 g the Pentateuch drafts use (1,100 shekels is about 12.7 kg). The English gives US pounds; Swahili readers measure in kilograms.

decisions.choice: "unos 13 kilos de plata" by default, "1100 siclos de plata" with the measures setting
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch terms set: measures are metric by default where the English converts, with the original unit as the alternative. 1,100 shekels at about 11.5 g each is about 12.7 kg, rounded as the English rounds ("about 28 pounds"). "Los jefes" for the rulers of the Philistines, the five lords of their cities (m1).

source.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר דְּלִילָה֙ אֶל־שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן הַגִּֽידָה־נָּ֣א לִ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה כֹּחֲךָ֣ גָד֑וֹל וּבַמֶּ֥ה תֵאָסֵ֖ר לְעַנּוֹתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Delilah to Samson, tell, please, to me in what your strength [is] great and with what you may be bound to humble you.

en.L: And Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me in what your great strength [lies], and with what you could be bound so as to subdue you."
en.B: So Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me what makes your strength so great, and what it would take to tie you up and subdue you."
en.R: So Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me the secret of your great strength. How could someone tie you up and make you helpless?"

sw.L: Naye Delila akamwambia Samsoni, "Tafadhali niambie nguvu zako nyingi [ziko] katika nini, na kwa kitu gani waweza kufungwa ili kukutiisha."
sw.B: Basi Delila alimwambia Samsoni, "Tafadhali niambie ni nini kinachokupa nguvu nyingi hivyo, na ingehitajika nini kukufunga na kukutiisha."
sw.R: Basi Delila alimwambia Samsoni, "Tafadhali niambie siri ya nguvu zako nyingi. Mtu angewezaje kukufunga na kukufanya usiweze kufanya lolote?"

es.L: Y Dalila dijo a Sansón: «Dime, te ruego, en qué [está] tu gran fuerza, y con qué podrías ser atado para someterte».
es.B: Entonces Dalila le dijo a Sansón: «Dime, por favor, de dónde te viene esa fuerza tan grande, y qué haría falta para atarte y someterte».
es.R: Entonces Dalila le dijo a Sansón: «Por favor, dime el secreto de tu gran fuerza. ¿Cómo podría alguien atarte y dejarte indefenso?».

decisions.choice: Delilah asks openly
decisions.reason: Her question repeats the rulers' words almost exactly (verse 5), even "to subdue you". She hides nothing of what she wants, yet Samson goes on playing with her.

decisions.choice: the secret of your great strength
decisions.reason: Readable says "secret", since she is asking where his strength comes from.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן אִם־יַאַסְרֻ֗נִי בְּשִׁבְעָ֛ה יְתָרִ֥ים לַחִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־חֹרָ֑בוּוְחָלִ֥יתִי וְהָיִ֖יתִי כְּאַחַ֥ד הָאָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her Samson, if they bind me with seven bowstrings fresh that not have been dried, and I will be weak and I will be like one of the man.

en.L: And Samson said to her, "If they bind me with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, then I will become weak and be like any [other] man."
en.B: Samson answered, "Suppose they tie me with seven fresh bowstrings that were never dried. Then I will become weak and be like any other man."
en.R: Samson told her, "If someone ties me up with seven fresh bowstrings that have not dried out yet, I will lose my strength. I will be as weak as anyone else."

sw.L: Naye Samsoni akamwambia, "Wakinifunga kwa kamba saba mbichi za upinde ambazo hazijakaushwa, nitakuwa dhaifu na kuwa kama mtu mwingine yeyote."
sw.B: Samsoni alimjibu, "Kama wangenifunga kwa kamba saba mbichi za upinde ambazo hazijawahi kukaushwa, ningekuwa dhaifu na kuwa kama mtu mwingine yeyote."
sw.R: Samsoni alimwambia, "Mtu akinifunga kwa kamba saba mbichi za upinde ambazo bado hazijakauka, nitapoteza nguvu zangu. Nitakuwa dhaifu kama mtu mwingine yeyote."

es.L: Y Sansón le dijo: «Si me atan con siete cuerdas de arco frescas que no se hayan secado, entonces me debilitaré y seré como cualquier [otro] hombre».
es.B: Sansón le respondió: «Si me atan con siete cuerdas de arco frescas, que nunca se hayan secado, me debilitaré y seré como cualquier otro hombre».
es.R: Sansón le dijo: «Si alguien me ata con siete cuerdas de arco frescas, que todavía no se hayan secado, perderé mi fuerza. Seré tan débil como cualquier otro».

decisions.choice: fresh bowstrings: cords of gut or sinew
decisions.reason: The word (yeter) is a cord: a bowstring (Psalm 11:2) or a tent cord (Job 4:21). "Fresh, not dried" points to cords made from animal gut or sinew, still moist and supple.

decisions.choice: seven: a full number
decisions.reason: Seven stands for completeness. His hair too is in seven braids (verses 13, 19), so the number of his lie points toward the truth.

decisions.choice: like any other man: an ordinary human being
decisions.reason: "Like one of mankind" means no stronger than anyone else.

decisions.choice: bowstrings
decisions.reason: "Bowstrings" names the commonest use of the word and shows what kind of cord it was (m1).

source.text: וַיַּעֲלוּ־לָ֞הּ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים שִׁבְעָ֛ה יְתָרִ֥ים לַחִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־חֹרָ֑בוּ וַתַּאַסְרֵ֖הוּ בָּהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And brought up to her [the] rulers of [the] Philistines seven bowstrings fresh that not had been dried, and she bound him with them.

en.L: And the rulers of the Philistines brought up to her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she bound him with them.
en.B: So the Philistine rulers brought up to her seven fresh bowstrings, never dried, and she tied him up with them.
en.R: So the Philistine rulers brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not dried out. And she tied Samson up with them.

sw.L: Nao watawala wa Wafilisti wakampandishia kamba saba mbichi za upinde ambazo hazijakaushwa, naye akamfunga kwa hizo.
sw.B: Basi watawala wa Wafilisti walimletea kamba saba mbichi za upinde zisizokaushwa, naye akamfunga kwa kamba hizo.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo watawala wa Wafilisti walimletea kamba saba mbichi za upinde ambazo hazijakauka. Naye akamfunga Samsoni kwa kamba hizo.

es.L: Y los jefes de los filisteos le subieron siete cuerdas de arco frescas que no se habían secado, y ella lo ató con ellas.
es.B: Así que los jefes filisteos le llevaron siete cuerdas de arco frescas, sin secar, y ella lo ató con ellas.
es.R: Entonces los jefes filisteos le llevaron siete cuerdas de arco frescas que no se habían secado. Y ella ató a Sansón con ellas.

decisions.choice: she bound him
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether Samson was awake or asleep, or how he let himself be tied. It moves straight to the test (verse 9).

source.text: וְהָאֹרֵ֗ב יֹשֵׁ֥ב לָהּ֙ בַּחֶ֔דֶר וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו פְּלִשְׁתִּ֥ים עָלֶ֖יךָ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיְנַתֵּק֙ אֶת־הַיְתָרִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִנָּתֵ֤ק פְּתִֽיל־הַנְּעֹ֨רֶת֙ בַּהֲרִיח֣וֹ אֵ֔שׁ וְלֹ֥א נוֹדַ֖ע כֹּחֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the ambush [was] sitting for her in the room. And she said to him, [the] Philistines [are] upon you, Samson! And he snapped the bowstrings as snaps a strand of the tow when it smells fire. And not was known his strength.

en.L: Now the ambush was waiting for her in the inner room. And she said to him, "The Philistines [are] upon you, Samson!" And he snapped the bowstrings as a strand of tow snaps when it smells fire. And his strength was not known.
en.B: She had men hidden in the inner room, waiting. Then she said to him, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" But he snapped the bowstrings as easily as a strand of flax fiber snaps at the touch of fire. So the secret of his strength was still not found out.
en.R: Some men were hiding in the inner room, waiting. Delilah shouted, "Samson! The Philistines are here to get you!" But Samson broke the bowstrings as easily as a thread breaks when a flame touches it. So no one found out the secret of his strength.

sw.L: Na waviziaji walikuwa wakimngoja katika chumba cha ndani. Naye akamwambia, "Wafilisti wako juu yako, Samsoni!" Naye akazikata zile kamba za upinde kama uzi wa katani ukatikavyo unapoguswa na moto. Wala nguvu zake hazikujulikana.
sw.B: Alikuwa amewaficha watu katika chumba cha ndani wakingoja. Kisha akamwambia, "Samsoni, Wafilisti wako juu yako!" Lakini alizikata zile kamba za upinde kwa urahisi kama uzi wa katani ukatikavyo unapoguswa na moto. Kwa hiyo siri ya nguvu zake bado haikujulikana.
sw.R: Watu fulani walikuwa wamejificha katika chumba cha ndani wakingoja. Delila alipiga kelele, "Samsoni! Wafilisti wamekuja kukukamata!" Lakini Samsoni alizikata zile kamba kwa urahisi kama uzi ukatikavyo unapoguswa na mwali wa moto. Kwa hiyo hakuna aliyejua siri ya nguvu zake.

es.L: Y la emboscada estaba esperando en el cuarto interior. Y ella le dijo: «¡Los filisteos [están] sobre ti, Sansón!». Y él rompió las cuerdas como se rompe una hebra de estopa cuando huele el fuego. Y no se supo [el secreto de] su fuerza.
es.B: Ella tenía hombres escondidos en el cuarto interior, al acecho. Entonces le dijo: «¡Sansón, los filisteos se te echan encima!». Pero él rompió las cuerdas con la misma facilidad con que se rompe una hebra de estopa al tocar el fuego. Así que el secreto de su fuerza siguió sin descubrirse.
es.R: Unos hombres estaban escondidos en el cuarto interior, esperando. Dalila gritó: «¡Sansón! ¡Los filisteos vienen por ti!». Pero Sansón rompió las cuerdas tan fácilmente como se rompe un hilo cuando lo toca una llama. Así que nadie descubrió el secreto de su fuerza.

decisions.choice: the ambush was waiting in the inner room
decisions.reason: "The ambush" means the men set to lie in wait. The room (cheder) is an inner room or bedroom (15:1), out of sight.

decisions.choice: as a strand of tow snaps when it smells fire
decisions.reason: Tow is the short, rough fibers left from flax. It catches fire at once. "When it smells fire" means when fire comes near it.

decisions.choice: his strength was not known: its source stayed hidden
decisions.reason: Everyone knew he was strong; what stayed unknown was where the strength came from and how to take it away.

decisions.choice: men hidden; the secret of his strength
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "the ambush" was (m1) and what was not known (m3).

source.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר דְּלִילָה֙ אֶל־שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן הִנֵּה֙ הֵתַ֣לְתָּ בִּ֔י וַתְּדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י כְּזָבִ֑ים עַתָּה֙ הַגִּֽידָה־נָּ֣א לִ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה תֵּאָסֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Delilah to Samson, look, you have mocked me and spoken to me lies; now tell, please, to me with what you may be bound.

en.L: And Delilah said to Samson, "Look, you have mocked me and told me lies. Now, please tell me with what you could be bound."
en.B: Then Delilah said to Samson, "You have made a fool of me and told me lies! Now please tell me what it would take to tie you up."
en.R: Delilah said to Samson, "You tricked me! You lied to me! Now please tell me. How can someone tie you up?"

sw.L: Naye Delila akamwambia Samsoni, "Tazama, umenidhihaki na kuniambia uongo. Sasa tafadhali niambie waweza kufungwa kwa kitu gani."
sw.B: Kisha Delila alimwambia Samsoni, "Umenifanya mjinga na kuniambia uongo! Sasa tafadhali niambie ingehitajika nini kukufunga."
sw.R: Delila alimwambia Samsoni, "Umenidanganya! Umeniambia uongo! Sasa tafadhali niambie. Mtu anawezaje kukufunga?"

es.L: Y Dalila dijo a Sansón: «He aquí, te has burlado de mí y me has dicho mentiras. Ahora, te ruego, dime con qué podrías ser atado».
es.B: Entonces Dalila le dijo a Sansón: «¡Te has burlado de mí y me has mentido! Ahora, por favor, dime qué haría falta para atarte».
es.R: Dalila le dijo a Sansón: «¡Me engañaste! ¡Me mentiste! Ahora, por favor, dímelo. ¿Cómo se te puede atar?».

decisions.choice: you have mocked me: you have made a fool of me
decisions.reason: The verb means to trifle with or deceive someone; Laban "cheated" Jacob with it (Genesis 31:7). Delilah complains of being lied to while she herself is lying to him.

decisions.choice: "Look" (L) is left out at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word draws attention to what follows. Balanced and Readable show that by the tone of her complaint instead.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אִם־אָס֤וֹר יַאַסְר֨וּנִי֙ בַּעֲבֹתִ֣ים חֲדָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־נַעֲשָׂ֥ה בָהֶ֖ם מְלָאכָ֑ה וְחָלִ֥יתִי וְהָיִ֖יתִי כְּאַחַ֥ד הָאָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to her, if binding they bind me with ropes new that not has been done with them work, and I will be weak and I will be like one of the man.

en.L: And he said to her, "If they really bind me with new ropes with which no work has been done, then I will become weak and be like any [other] man."
en.B: He said to her, "If they tie me up tightly with new ropes that have never been used for work, I will become weak and be like any other man."
en.R: He said to her, "If someone ties me up tightly with brand-new ropes, ones never used for work, I will lose my strength. I will be like anyone else."

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Wakinifunga kweli kwa kamba mpya ambazo hazijafanyiwa kazi yoyote, nitakuwa dhaifu na kuwa kama mtu mwingine yeyote."
sw.B: Akamwambia, "Wakinifunga kwa nguvu kwa kamba mpya ambazo hazijawahi kutumika kwa kazi yoyote, nitakuwa dhaifu na kuwa kama mtu mwingine yeyote."
sw.R: Akamwambia, "Mtu akinifunga kwa nguvu kwa kamba mpya kabisa, ambazo hazijawahi kutumika kwa kazi, nitapoteza nguvu zangu. Nitakuwa kama mtu mwingine yeyote."

es.L: Y él le dijo: «Si de veras me atan con cuerdas nuevas con las que no se haya hecho trabajo, entonces me debilitaré y seré como cualquier [otro] hombre».
es.B: Él le dijo: «Si me atan bien fuerte con cuerdas nuevas que nunca se hayan usado para trabajar, me debilitaré y seré como cualquier otro hombre».
es.R: Él le dijo: «Si alguien me ata bien fuerte con cuerdas nuevas, que nunca se hayan usado para trabajar, perderé mi fuerza. Seré como cualquier otro».

decisions.choice: if they really bind me: tie me up firmly
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled ("binding they bind"), a common Hebrew way of stressing an action: tied up properly and tight.

decisions.choice: new ropes: they had failed before
decisions.reason: The men of Judah had bound Samson with two new ropes, and he broke them like burnt flax (15:13-14). Delilah may not know it; the reader does.

decisions.choice: really (L); tightly (B, R)
decisions.reason: The doubled verb (m1) is shown by an adverb.

source.text: וַתִּקַּ֣ח דְּלִילָה֩ עֲבֹתִ֨ים חֲדָשִׁ֜ים וַתַּאַסְרֵ֣הוּ בָהֶ֗ם וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֤ים עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן וְהָאֹרֵ֖ב יֹשֵׁ֣ב בֶּחָ֑דֶר וַֽיְנַתְּקֵ֛ם מֵעַ֥ל זְרֹעֹתָ֖יו כַּחֽוּט׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Delilah ropes new and bound him with them, and she said to him, [the] Philistines [are] upon you, Samson! And the ambush [was] sitting in the room. And he snapped them from upon his arms like thread.

en.L: So Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them, and said to him, "The Philistines [are] upon you, Samson!" And the ambush was waiting in the inner room. And he snapped them off his arms like a thread.
en.B: So Delilah took new ropes and tied him up with them. Then she said to him, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" Men were hidden in the inner room, waiting. But he snapped the ropes off his arms like thread.
en.R: So Delilah got some new ropes and tied him up with them. Men were hiding in the inner room again. Delilah shouted, "Samson! The Philistines are here to get you!" But he broke the ropes off his arms as if they were thread.

sw.L: Basi Delila akatwaa kamba mpya, akamfunga kwa hizo, akamwambia, "Wafilisti wako juu yako, Samsoni!" Na waviziaji walikuwa wakingoja katika chumba cha ndani. Naye akazikata kutoka mikononi mwake kama uzi.
sw.B: Basi Delila alichukua kamba mpya, akamfunga kwa kamba hizo. Kisha akamwambia, "Samsoni, Wafilisti wako juu yako!" Watu walikuwa wamejificha katika chumba cha ndani, wakingoja. Lakini alizikata zile kamba mikononi mwake kama uzi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Delila alileta kamba mpya, akamfunga kwa hizo. Watu walikuwa wamejificha tena katika chumba cha ndani. Delila alipiga kelele, "Samsoni! Wafilisti wamekuja kukukamata!" Lakini alizikata zile kamba mikononi mwake kana kwamba zilikuwa uzi.

es.L: Y tomó Dalila cuerdas nuevas y lo ató con ellas, y le dijo: «¡Los filisteos [están] sobre ti, Sansón!». Y la emboscada estaba esperando en el cuarto interior. Y él las rompió de sobre sus brazos como un hilo.
es.B: Así que Dalila tomó cuerdas nuevas y lo ató con ellas. Luego le dijo: «¡Sansón, los filisteos se te echan encima!». Había hombres escondidos en el cuarto interior, al acecho. Pero él rompió las cuerdas de sus brazos como si fueran hilo.
es.R: Entonces Dalila consiguió cuerdas nuevas y lo ató con ellas. Otra vez había hombres escondidos en el cuarto interior. Dalila gritó: «¡Sansón! ¡Los filisteos vienen por ti!». Pero él se quitó las cuerdas de los brazos rompiéndolas como si fueran hilo.

decisions.choice: the ambush was waiting: already there
decisions.reason: The clause about the men in hiding comes after her cry, but it describes how things stood: they had been waiting all along, as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: like thread
decisions.reason: A single spun thread, the weakest of cords. The test ends as the first did (verse 9).

decisions.choice: Men were hiding ... again, before her shout
decisions.reason: Readable puts the background first (m1), so the order of events is clear.

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר דְּלִילָ֜ה אֶל־שִׁמְשׁ֗וֹן עַד־הֵ֜נָּה הֵתַ֤לְתָּ בִּי֙ וַתְּדַבֵּ֤ר אֵלַי֙ כְּזָבִ֔ים הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה תֵּאָסֵ֑ר וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אִם־תַּאַרְגִ֗י אֶת־שֶׁ֛בַע מַחְלְפ֥וֹת רֹאשִׁ֖י עִם־הַמַּסָּֽכֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Delilah to Samson, until now you have mocked me and spoken to me lies; tell to me with what you may be bound. And he said to her, if you weave [the] seven braids of my head with the web.

en.L: And Delilah said to Samson, "Until now you have mocked me and told me lies. Tell me with what you could be bound." And he said to her, "If you weave the seven braids of my head with the web."
en.B: Then Delilah said to Samson, "All this time you have been making a fool of me and telling me lies. Tell me what it would take to tie you up." He answered, "Weave the seven braids of my head into the fabric on the loom."
en.R: Delilah said to Samson, "You keep tricking me and telling me lies! Tell me how someone can tie you up." Samson said, "My hair is in seven braids. Weave them into the cloth on your loom."

sw.L: Naye Delila akamwambia Samsoni, "Mpaka sasa umenidhihaki na kuniambia uongo. Niambie waweza kufungwa kwa kitu gani." Naye akamwambia, "Ukisuka mashungi saba ya kichwa changu pamoja na kitambaa cha mfumi."
sw.B: Kisha Delila alimwambia Samsoni, "Muda wote huu umekuwa ukinifanya mjinga na kuniambia uongo. Niambie ingehitajika nini kukufunga." Akamjibu, "Suka mashungi saba ya kichwa changu ndani ya kitambaa kilicho kwenye kitanda cha kufumia."
sw.R: Delila alimwambia Samsoni, "Unaendelea kunidanganya na kuniambia uongo! Niambie mtu anawezaje kukufunga." Samsoni alisema, "Nywele zangu zimesukwa mashungi saba. Yasuke ndani ya kitambaa kilicho kwenye kitanda chako cha kufumia."

es.L: Y Dalila dijo a Sansón: «Hasta ahora te has burlado de mí y me has dicho mentiras. Dime con qué podrías ser atado». Y él le dijo: «Si tejes las siete trenzas de mi cabeza con la urdimbre».
es.B: Entonces Dalila le dijo a Sansón: «Todo este tiempo te has estado burlando de mí y me has dicho mentiras. Dime qué haría falta para atarte». Él le respondió: «Teje las siete trenzas de mi cabeza en la tela del telar».
es.R: Dalila le dijo a Sansón: «¡Sigues engañándome y diciéndome mentiras! Dime cómo se te puede atar». Sansón le dijo: «Mi pelo está en siete trenzas. Téjelas en la tela de tu telar».

decisions.choice: the shorter Hebrew text
alternatives: the longer text of the ancient Greek translation
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence stops after "if you weave the seven braids of my head with the web" and never says what would happen; verse 14 goes straight to "she fastened [it] with the pin". The ancient Greek translation has a longer text here, roughly: "... with the web, and fasten [it] with the pin into the wall, then I will become weak and be like any other man. And while he slept, Delilah took the seven braids of his head and wove them into the web." It then reads in verse 14 "and she fastened [it] with the pin into the wall". The longer text follows the pattern of verses 7-8 and 11-12, where each lie is followed by its test, and a copyist's eye could easily have jumped from one "web" to the next and dropped a line. The meaning of the story does not change, only how fully it is told. This draft follows the Hebrew and notes the longer reading. The wording of the Greek is given from general knowledge and must be checked against its manuscripts before review.

decisions.choice: weave ... with the web: on a loom
decisions.reason: The web (massekhet) is the cloth on the loom, the warp threads with the weaving in progress. Samson's long hair would be worked into it like thread, pinning his head to the loom.

decisions.choice: the seven braids of my head
decisions.reason: His hair had never been cut (13:5) and was kept in seven locks or braids. With this answer he comes close to the truth: for the first time his hair is the subject (verse 17).

decisions.choice: until now: all this time
decisions.reason: Delilah complains that he has lied every time so far.

decisions.choice: Weave the seven braids ...: an instruction
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "if" with no "then" clause (m1). Balanced and Readable put his words as an instruction, which gives the same sense without leaving the sentence hanging; Literal keeps the bare "if".

source.text: וַתִּתְקַע֙ בַּיָּתֵ֔ד וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו פְּלִשְׁתִּ֥ים עָלֶ֖יךָ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיִּיקַץ֙ מִשְּׁנָת֔וֹ וַיִּסַּ֛ע אֶת־הַיְתַ֥ד הָאֶ֖רֶג וְאֶת־הַמַּסָּֽכֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And she fastened with the pin, and she said to him, [the] Philistines [are] upon you, Samson! And he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the loom and the web.

en.L: And she fastened [it] with the pin, and said to him, "The Philistines [are] upon you, Samson!" And he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the loom, and the web.
en.B: So she wove his hair in and fastened it tight with the pin, and said to him, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" He woke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the loom along with the web.
en.R: So Delilah wove his hair into the cloth and fastened it tight with the pin. Then she shouted, "Samson! The Philistines are here to get you!" Samson woke up. He pulled out the pin of the loom, and the cloth with it.

sw.L: Naye akakaza [kwa] kigingi, akamwambia, "Wafilisti wako juu yako, Samsoni!" Naye akaamka usingizini mwake, akakingoa kigingi cha kitanda cha kufumia, na kile kitambaa.
sw.B: Basi aliyasuka mashungi yake ndani ya kitambaa, akayakaza kwa kigingi, akamwambia, "Samsoni, Wafilisti wako juu yako!" Akaamka usingizini, akakingoa kigingi cha kitanda cha kufumia pamoja na kitambaa.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Delila aliyasuka mashungi yake ndani ya kitambaa, akayakaza kwa kigingi. Kisha alipiga kelele, "Samsoni! Wafilisti wamekuja kukukamata!" Samsoni aliamka. Alikingoa kigingi cha kitanda cha kufumia, pamoja na kitambaa.

es.L: Y [la] sujetó con la estaca, y le dijo: «¡Los filisteos [están] sobre ti, Sansón!». Y él despertó de su sueño y arrancó la estaca del telar, y la urdimbre.
es.B: Ella tejió el cabello en la tela, la sujetó bien con la estaca y le dijo: «¡Sansón, los filisteos se te echan encima!». Él despertó de su sueño y arrancó la estaca del telar junto con la tela.
es.R: Entonces Dalila tejió el pelo de Sansón en la tela y la sujetó bien con la estaca. Luego gritó: «¡Sansón! ¡Los filisteos vienen por ti!». Sansón se despertó. Arrancó la estaca del telar, y la tela con ella.

decisions.choice: she fastened [it] with the pin
decisions.reason: As at verse 13: the Hebrew does not say what she fastened, and the ancient Greek translation has a longer text that tells how she wove his hair into the web while he slept and pinned it "into the wall". The Hebrew implies the same: he was asleep, and the web came away with his hair.

decisions.choice: the pin
decisions.reason: The word (yated) is a peg or pin; it is the tent peg Jael drove through Sisera's head (4:21-22). Here it is the weaving pin that held the work tight on the loom.

decisions.choice: the pin of the loom, and the web
alternatives: the pin, the loom and the web
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists "the pin, the loom, and the web". It is read as the loom's pin together with the woven cloth: he pulled his head free and tore it all away.

decisions.choice: she wove his hair in / wove his hair into the cloth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what verse 13 and his pulling out the web imply: she did weave his hair in before pinning it (m1). This is not taken from the longer Greek text; the Hebrew story needs it.

source.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אֵ֚יךְ תֹּאמַ֣ר אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ וְלִבְּךָ֖ אֵ֣ין אִתִּ֑י זֶ֣ה שָׁלֹ֤שׁ פְּעָמִים֙ הֵתַ֣לְתָּ בִּ֔י וְלֹא־הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה כֹּחֲךָ֥ גָדֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said to him, how will you say, I love you, and your heart not [is] with me? These three times you have mocked me and not told me in what your strength [is] great.

en.L: And she said to him, "How can you say, 'I love you,' and your heart is not with me? These three times you have mocked me, and you have not told me in what your great strength [lies]."
en.B: Then she said to him, "How can you tell me, 'I love you,' while you keep your heart from me? Three times now you have made a fool of me, and you still have not told me what makes your strength so great."
en.R: Then she said to him, "How can you say that you love me? You do not trust me with what is in your heart. Three times now you have made a fool of me. You still have not told me why you are so strong."

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Wawezaje kusema, 'Nakupenda,' na moyo wako hauko pamoja nami? Mara hizi tatu umenidhihaki, wala hujaniambia nguvu zako nyingi [ziko] katika nini."
sw.B: Kisha alimwambia, "Wawezaje kuniambia, 'Nakupenda,' na huku unanificha moyo wako? Mara tatu sasa umenifanya mjinga, wala bado hujaniambia ni nini kinachokupa nguvu nyingi hivyo."
sw.R: Kisha alimwambia, "Wawezaje kusema kwamba unanipenda? Huniamini kuniambia yaliyo moyoni mwako. Mara tatu sasa umenifanya mjinga. Bado hujaniambia kwa nini una nguvu nyingi hivyo."

es.L: Y ella le dijo: «¿Cómo puedes decir: “Te amo”, si tu corazón no está conmigo? Estas tres veces te has burlado de mí, y no me has dicho en qué [está] tu gran fuerza».
es.B: Entonces ella le dijo: «¿Cómo puedes decirme “Te amo”, si me escondes tu corazón? Ya van tres veces que te burlas de mí, y todavía no me has dicho de dónde te viene esa fuerza tan grande».
es.R: Entonces ella le dijo: «¿Cómo puedes decir que me amas? No me confías lo que hay en tu corazón. Ya van tres veces que te burlas de mí. Todavía no me has dicho por qué eres tan fuerte».

decisions.choice: your heart is not with me: you do not open your mind to me
decisions.reason: The heart is the inner self, the thoughts and will. A heart "not with" someone holds back from them. When he finally gives in, he tells her "all his heart" (verses 17-18).

decisions.choice: How can you say, 'I love you'?
decisions.reason: His wife at Timnah used the same weapon: "You only hate me; you do not love me" (14:16), and she too wore him down with tears for days.

decisions.choice: keep your heart from me (B); do not trust me with what is in your heart (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m1); Literal keeps it.

source.text: וַ֠יְהִי כִּֽי־הֵצִ֨יקָה לּ֧וֹ בִדְבָרֶ֛יהָ כָּל־הַיָּמִ֖ים וַתְּאַֽלֲצֵ֑הוּ וַתִּקְצַ֥ר נַפְשׁ֖וֹ לָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was when she pressed him with her words all the days and urged him, and was short his soul to die.

en.L: And it came about, when she pressed him with her words every day and urged him, that his soul was short to the point of death.
en.B: Day after day she kept pressing him with her words and pleading with him, until he was weary to death of it.
en.R: Day after day she kept asking him and begging him. At last Samson was so tired of it that he felt he would die.

sw.L: Ikawa alipomsumbua kwa maneno yake kila siku na kumsihi, roho yake ikadhikika hata kufa.
sw.B: Siku baada ya siku aliendelea kumsumbua kwa maneno yake na kumsihi, mpaka akachoka hata kutaka kufa.
sw.R: Siku baada ya siku aliendelea kumwuliza na kumsihi. Hatimaye Samsoni alichoka mno hata akajiona kana kwamba atakufa.

es.L: Y sucedió que, como ella lo presionaba con sus palabras todos los días y lo apremiaba, su alma se angustió hasta la muerte.
es.B: Día tras día ella lo presionaba con sus palabras y le insistía, hasta que él se hartó a morir.
es.R: Día tras día ella le preguntaba y le rogaba. Al final Sansón estaba tan cansado de todo aquello que sentía que se iba a morir.

decisions.choice: his soul was short to the point of death
decisions.reason: To be "short of soul" is to lose patience, to be unable to bear something any longer (Numbers 21:4; Judges 10:16). "To death" makes it extreme: he was worn out completely.

decisions.choice: urged him
decisions.reason: A rare verb meaning to press or push someone hard. With "pressed him" it shows how steady her pressure was.

decisions.choice: weary to death of it (B); so tired of it that he felt he would die (R)
alternatives: his soul was vexed to death
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "short of soul" means (m1).

source.text: וַיַּגֶּד־לָ֣הּ אֶת־כָּל־לִבּ֗וֹ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מוֹרָה֙ לֹֽא־עָלָ֣ה עַל־רֹאשִׁ֔י כִּֽי־נְזִ֧יר אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֲנִ֖י מִבֶּ֣טֶן אִמִּ֑י אִם־גֻּלַּ֨חְתִּי֙ וְסָ֣ר מִמֶּ֣נִּי כֹחִ֔י וְחָלִ֥יתִי וְהָיִ֖יתִי כְּכָל־הָאָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he told her all his heart and said to her, a razor not has come up on my head, for a Nazirite of God I [am] from [the] womb of my mother; if I am shaved, and will depart from me my strength, and I will be weak and I will be like all the man.

en.L: And he told her all his heart and said to her, "A razor has not come up on my head, for I [am] a Nazirite of God from my mother's womb. If I am shaved, then my strength will leave me, and I will become weak and be like any [other] man."
en.B: So he told her everything that was in his heart. "No razor has ever touched my head," he said to her, "because from my mother's womb I have been set apart to God as a Nazirite. If my head were shaved, my strength would leave me, and I would become weak and be like any other man."
en.R: So Samson told her his whole secret. He said, "My hair has never been cut. I have been a Nazirite since before I was born. That means I was set apart to serve God. If someone shaved my head, my strength would leave me. I would be as weak as anyone else."

sw.L: Naye akamwambia yote yaliyo moyoni mwake, akamwambia, "Wembe haujapita juu ya kichwa changu, kwa maana mimi [ni] Mnadhiri wa Mungu tangu tumboni mwa mama yangu. Nikinyolewa, nguvu zangu zitaniacha, nami nitakuwa dhaifu na kuwa kama mtu mwingine yeyote."
sw.B: Basi alimweleza yote yaliyokuwa moyoni mwake. Akamwambia, "Wembe haujawahi kugusa kichwa changu, kwa sababu tangu tumboni mwa mama yangu nimetengwa kwa ajili ya Mungu kama Mnadhiri. Kama kichwa changu kingenyolewa, nguvu zangu zingeniacha, nami ningekuwa dhaifu kama mtu mwingine yeyote."
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Samsoni alimwambia siri yake yote. Alisema, "Nywele zangu hazijawahi kukatwa. Nimekuwa Mnadhiri tangu kabla sijazaliwa. Maana yake nimetengwa ili kumtumikia Mungu. Mtu akininyoa kichwa, nguvu zangu zitaniacha. Nitakuwa dhaifu kama mtu mwingine yeyote."

es.L: Y le declaró todo su corazón y le dijo: «Navaja no ha subido sobre mi cabeza, porque nazareo de Dios [soy] desde el vientre de mi madre. Si soy rapado, mi fuerza se apartará de mí, y me debilitaré y seré como cualquier [otro] hombre».
es.B: Así que le contó todo lo que había en su corazón. «Nunca ha pasado navaja por mi cabeza —le dijo—, porque desde el vientre de mi madre he sido consagrado a Dios como nazareo. Si me raparan la cabeza, la fuerza me abandonaría, y me debilitaría y sería como cualquier otro hombre».
es.R: Así que Sansón le contó todo su secreto. Le dijo: «Nunca me han cortado el pelo. Soy nazareo desde antes de nacer. Eso quiere decir que fui apartado para servir a Dios. Si alguien me rapara la cabeza, perdería mi fuerza. Sería tan débil como cualquier otro».

decisions.choice: a Nazirite of God
decisions.reason: A Nazirite was a person set apart to God by a vow: no razor on the head, no wine or grape products, no touching a dead body (Numbers 6:1-21). Most took the vow for a time; Samson was given to it for life before his birth (13:5, 7).

decisions.choice: if I am shaved, my strength will leave me
decisions.reason: The strength was not in the hair as such. The uncut hair was the sign that he belonged to God, and the strength came from the Spirit of the LORD (14:6, 19; 15:14). When the sign is gone, the narrator says, the LORD had left him (verse 20).

decisions.choice: he told her all his heart: the whole truth
decisions.reason: He held nothing back. The same words return in verse 18, where Delilah sees that this time he has told her everything.

decisions.choice: That means I was set apart to serve God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word Nazirite (m1). "Since before I was born" gives the sense of "from my mother's womb".

source.text: וַתֵּ֣רֶא דְלִילָ֗הכִּֽי־הִגִּ֣יד לָהּ֮ אֶת־כָּל־לִבּוֹ֒ וַתִּשְׁלַ֡ח וַתִּקְרָא֩ לְסַרְנֵ֨י פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים לֵאמֹר֙ עֲל֣וּ הַפַּ֔עַם כִּֽי־הִגִּ֥יד לִ֖י אֶת־כָּל־לִבּ֑וֹ וְעָל֤וּ אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיַּעֲל֥וּ הַכֶּ֖סֶף בְּיָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Delilah that he had told her all his heart, and she sent and called to [the] rulers of [the] Philistines, saying, come up this time, for he has told me all his heart. And came up to her [the] rulers of [the] Philistines and brought up the silver in their hand.

en.L: And Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, and she sent and called the rulers of the Philistines, saying, "Come up this once, for he has told me all his heart." And the rulers of the Philistines came up to her and brought up the silver in their hand.
en.B: When Delilah saw that he had told her everything in his heart, she sent word to the rulers of the Philistines: "Come up just once more, for he has told me everything." So the rulers of the Philistines came up to her, bringing the silver with them.
en.R: Delilah could tell that this time Samson had told her the truth. So she sent a message to the Philistine rulers. She said, "Come back one more time. He has told me everything." So the rulers came, and they brought the silver with them to pay her.

sw.L: Naye Delila akaona ya kuwa amemwambia yote yaliyo moyoni mwake, akatuma akawaita watawala wa Wafilisti, akisema, "Pandeni mara hii moja, kwa maana ameniambia yote yaliyo moyoni mwake." Nao watawala wa Wafilisti wakapanda kwake, wakaileta ile fedha mikononi mwao.
sw.B: Delila alipoona kwamba amemweleza yote yaliyokuwa moyoni mwake, alituma ujumbe kwa watawala wa Wafilisti: "Pandeni mara moja tena, kwa maana ameniambia kila kitu." Basi watawala wa Wafilisti walipanda kwake, wakiileta ile fedha pamoja nao.
sw.R: Delila alitambua kwamba safari hii Samsoni amemwambia ukweli. Kwa hiyo alituma ujumbe kwa watawala wa Wafilisti. Alisema, "Njooni mara moja tena. Ameniambia kila kitu." Basi watawala walikuja, wakaleta ile fedha pamoja nao ili wamlipe.

es.L: Y vio Dalila que él le había declarado todo su corazón, y envió a llamar a los jefes de los filisteos, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Suban|Subid}} esta vez, porque me ha declarado todo su corazón». Y los jefes de los filisteos subieron a ella y trajeron la plata en su mano.
es.B: Cuando Dalila vio que él le había contado todo lo que tenía en el corazón, mandó a llamar a los jefes de los filisteos: «{{plural_you:Suban|Subid}} solo una vez más, porque me lo ha contado todo». Entonces los jefes de los filisteos subieron a verla, trayendo consigo la plata.
es.R: Dalila se dio cuenta de que esta vez Sansón le había dicho la verdad. Así que les mandó un mensaje a los jefes filisteos. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vuelvan|Volved}} una vez más. Me lo ha contado todo». Entonces los jefes vinieron, y trajeron consigo la plata para pagarle.

decisions.choice: he has told me (in Delilah's message)
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text say "he has told her", but the reading marked in the margin for reading aloud is "he has told me". Since these are Delilah's own words, "me" fits; the written form may have been copied from the first half of the verse.

decisions.choice: Delilah saw: she could tell he spoke the truth
decisions.reason: The text does not say how she knew. This answer was different: it spoke of God and of his birth, not only of cords and ropes.

decisions.choice: they brought the silver in their hand
decisions.reason: The rulers come ready to pay what they had promised (verse 5).

decisions.choice: to pay her
decisions.reason: Readable says what the silver was for (m3).

source.text: וַתְּיַשְּׁנֵ֨הוּ֙ עַל־בִּרְכֶּ֔יהָ וַתִּקְרָ֣א לָאִ֔ישׁ וַתְּגַלַּ֕ח אֶת־שֶׁ֖בַע מַחְלְפ֣וֹת רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַתָּ֨חֶל֙ לְעַנּוֹת֔וֹ וַיָּ֥סַר כֹּח֖וֹ מֵעָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And she made him sleep on her knees and called for the man and she shaved [the] seven braids of his head, and she began to humble him, and departed his strength from upon him.

en.L: And she made him sleep on her knees, and called for a man, and she shaved off the seven braids of his head. And she began to subdue him, and his strength left him.
en.B: She lulled him to sleep on her lap and called for a man, and she had the seven braids of his head shaved off. Then she began to subdue him, and his strength had left him.
en.R: Delilah got Samson to fall asleep with his head on her lap. Then she called for a man to come and shave off the seven braids of his hair. Then Delilah began to mistreat him, and he was helpless. His strength was gone.

sw.L: Naye akamlaza usingizi magotini pake, akamwita mtu, naye akayanyoa mashungi saba ya kichwa chake. Naye akaanza kumtiisha, na nguvu zake zikamwacha.
sw.B: Alimbembeleza mpaka akalala magotini pake, akamwita mtu, naye akayanyoa mashungi saba ya kichwa chake. Kisha alianza kumtiisha, kwa maana nguvu zake zilikuwa zimemwacha.
sw.R: Delila alimfanya Samsoni alale akiwa ameweka kichwa chake magotini pake. Kisha alimwita mtu aje kumnyoa mashungi saba ya nywele zake. Kisha Delila alianza kumtesa, naye hakuweza kujitetea. Nguvu zake zilikuwa zimekwisha.

es.L: Y lo hizo dormir sobre sus rodillas, y llamó a un hombre, y rapó las siete trenzas de su cabeza. Y comenzó a someterlo, y su fuerza se apartó de él.
es.B: Ella lo hizo dormirse en su regazo, llamó a un hombre e hizo que le raparan las siete trenzas de la cabeza. Entonces comenzó a someterlo, y su fuerza lo había abandonado.
es.R: Dalila hizo que Sansón se durmiera con la cabeza en su regazo. Luego llamó a un hombre para que le cortara las siete trenzas del pelo. Después Dalila comenzó a maltratarlo, y él no pudo defenderse. Su fuerza había desaparecido.

decisions.choice: on her knees: in her lap
decisions.reason: He fell asleep with his head on her lap, trusting her.

decisions.choice: she shaved: through the man she called
decisions.reason: The verb "shaved" is hers, but she had called a man for the task; the act was done at her command.

decisions.choice: she began to subdue him
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verses 5-6: to bring low, overpower, mistreat. The ancient Greek translation reads "he began to be brought low", making Samson the subject; the Hebrew makes Delilah the one who begins to break him.

decisions.choice: had ... shaved off (B); called for a man to come and shave (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who used the razor (m2).

source.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר פְּלִשְׁתִּ֥ים עָלֶ֖יךָ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיִּקַ֣ץ מִשְּׁנָת֗וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵצֵ֞א כְּפַ֤עַם בְּפַ֨עַם֙ וְאִנָּעֵ֔ר וְהוּא֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה סָ֥ר מֵעָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, [the] Philistines [are] upon you, Samson! And he awoke from his sleep and said, I will go out as time in time and I will shake free. And he not knew that YHWH had departed from upon him.

en.L: And she said, "The Philistines [are] upon you, Samson!" And he awoke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as time after time, and shake myself free." But he did not know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had departed from him.
en.B: Then she said, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" He woke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as I did the other times and shake myself loose." But he did not know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had left him.
en.R: Then she shouted, "Samson! The Philistines are here to get you!" Samson woke up. He said to himself, "I will get away, just like before. I will shake myself loose." But he did not know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had left him.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Wafilisti wako juu yako, Samsoni!" Naye akaamka usingizini mwake, akasema, "Nitatoka kama mara zile nyingine, na kujinasua." Lakini hakujua ya kuwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemwacha.
sw.B: Kisha alisema, "Samsoni, Wafilisti wako juu yako!" Aliamka usingizini, akasema, "Nitatoka kama nilivyofanya mara zile nyingine na kujinasua." Lakini hakujua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemwacha.
sw.R: Kisha alipiga kelele, "Samsoni! Wafilisti wamekuja kukukamata!" Samsoni aliamka. Alijisemea, "Nitaponyoka, kama zamani. Nitajinasua." Lakini hakujua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemwacha.

es.L: Y ella dijo: «¡Los filisteos [están] sobre ti, Sansón!». Y él despertó de su sueño y dijo: «Saldré como las otras veces, y me sacudiré». Pero él no sabía que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se había apartado de él.
es.B: Entonces ella le dijo: «¡Sansón, los filisteos se te echan encima!». Él despertó de su sueño y dijo: «Saldré como las otras veces y me soltaré». Pero no sabía que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había abandonado.
es.R: Entonces ella gritó: «¡Sansón! ¡Los filisteos vienen por ti!». Sansón se despertó. Pensó: «Me escaparé, igual que antes. Me soltaré de un tirón». Pero no sabía que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había abandonado.

decisions.choice: the LORD had departed from him
decisions.reason: This is the real loss. Samson's strength came when the Spirit of the LORD rushed on him (14:6, 19; 15:14); with the sign of his vow gone, the LORD left him. The same words are later used of Saul (1 Samuel 16:14; 18:12).

decisions.choice: as time after time: as on the other occasions
decisions.reason: He expects things to go as they did each time before (verses 9, 12, 14).

decisions.choice: he said: possibly to himself
decisions.reason: The words may be spoken aloud or only in his mind; Hebrew "said" covers both.

decisions.choice: He said to himself
decisions.reason: Readable takes his words as his thoughts (m3); Literal and Balanced keep "said".

source.text: וַיֹּאחֲז֣וּהוּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַֽיְנַקְּר֖וּ אֶת־עֵינָ֑יו וַיּוֹרִ֨ידוּ אוֹת֜וֹ עַזָּ֗תָה וַיַּאַסְר֨וּהוּ֙ בַּֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֔יִם וַיְהִ֥י טוֹחֵ֖ן בְּבֵ֥ית הָאֲסוּרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And seized him [the] Philistines and gouged out his eyes and brought him down to Gaza and bound him with the bronze fetters, and he was grinding in [the] house of the prisoners.

en.L: And the Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza and bound him with bronze fetters, and he was grinding in the house of the prisoners.
en.B: The Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes. They took him down to Gaza and bound him with bronze shackles, and he was set to grinding grain in the prison.
en.R: The Philistines grabbed Samson and put out his eyes. They took him down to Gaza and put bronze chains on him. They made him grind grain in the prison.

sw.L: Nao Wafilisti wakamkamata, wakamng'oa macho, wakamshusha Gaza, wakamfunga kwa pingu za shaba, naye akawa akisaga katika nyumba ya wafungwa.
sw.B: Wafilisti walimkamata, wakamng'oa macho. Walimpeleka Gaza, wakamfunga kwa pingu za shaba, naye akawekwa kusaga nafaka gerezani.
sw.R: Wafilisti walimkamata Samsoni, wakamtoboa macho. Walimpeleka Gaza, wakamfunga minyororo ya shaba. Walimfanya asage nafaka gerezani.

es.L: Y los filisteos lo agarraron y le sacaron los ojos, y lo bajaron a Gaza y lo ataron con cadenas de bronce, y molía en la casa de los presos.
es.B: Los filisteos lo apresaron y le sacaron los ojos. Lo llevaron a Gaza, lo sujetaron con cadenas de bronce y lo pusieron a moler grano en la cárcel.
es.R: Los filisteos agarraron a Sansón y le sacaron los ojos. Lo llevaron a Gaza y le pusieron cadenas de bronce. Lo obligaron a moler grano en la cárcel.

decisions.choice: they gouged out his eyes
decisions.reason: Blinding was done to prisoners of war to make them helpless and to shame them (2 Kings 25:7). Samson's story began with what he saw and wanted (14:1-3); now his eyes are taken.

decisions.choice: grinding in the prison
decisions.reason: Grinding grain with a hand mill was the lowest work, done by slaves and women (Exodus 11:5; Isaiah 47:2). For a warrior it was deep humiliation.

decisions.choice: bronze fetters: a pair of shackles
decisions.reason: The word is "bronze" in a form meaning a pair: two linked bronze bands for the hands or feet.

decisions.choice: grain
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what he was grinding, which the Hebrew leaves understood (m2).

source.text: וַיָּ֧חֶל שְׂעַר־רֹאשׁ֛וֹ לְצַמֵּ֖חַ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר גֻּלָּֽח׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And began [the] hair of his head to grow as when it had been shaved.

en.L: And the hair of his head began to grow after it had been shaved.
en.B: But the hair of his head began to grow again after it had been shaved.
en.R: But Samson's hair began to grow back after it had been shaved off.

sw.L: Na nywele za kichwa chake zikaanza kuota baada ya kunyolewa.
sw.B: Lakini nywele za kichwa chake zilianza kuota tena baada ya kunyolewa.
sw.R: Lakini nywele za Samsoni zilianza kuota tena baada ya kunyolewa.

es.L: Y el cabello de su cabeza comenzó a crecer después de que fue rapado.
es.B: Pero el cabello de su cabeza empezó a crecer de nuevo después de haber sido rapado.
es.R: Pero el pelo de Sansón comenzó a crecer otra vez después de que se lo raparon.

decisions.choice: after it had been shaved: from the time it was shaved
alternatives: just as it had been before it was shaved
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "as soon as" or "after": from the day it was cut, it started growing back.

decisions.choice: his hair began to grow: a hint of what is coming
decisions.reason: The narrator tells the reader something the Philistines ignore. It does not say his strength came back with the hair; in verse 28 Samson asks the LORD for it.

source.text: וְסַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים נֶֽאֱסְפוּ֙לִזְבֹּ֧חַ זֶֽבַח־גָּד֛וֹל לְדָג֥וֹן אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם וּלְשִׂמְחָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ נָתַ֤ן אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ בְּיָדֵ֔נוּ אֵ֖ת שִׁמְשׁ֥וֹן אוֹיְבֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rulers of [the] Philistines gathered to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and for rejoicing, and they said, has given our god into our hand Samson our enemy.

en.L: And the rulers of the Philistines gathered to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god, and to rejoice, \q and they said, "Our god has given into our hand \q Samson our enemy."
en.B: Now the rulers of the Philistines assembled to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon and to celebrate. \q They said, "Our god has given into our hands \q Samson our enemy."
en.R: The Philistine rulers came together for a great festival. They offered sacrifices to their god Dagon and celebrated. \q They said, "Our god has handed Samson over to us, \q Samson our enemy!"

sw.L: Nao watawala wa Wafilisti wakakusanyika ili kumtolea Dagoni mungu wao dhabihu kubwa, na kufurahi, \q wakasema, "Mungu wetu amemtia mkononi mwetu \q Samsoni adui yetu."
sw.B: Basi watawala wa Wafilisti walikusanyika ili kumtolea mungu wao Dagoni dhabihu kubwa na kusherehekea. \q Walisema, "Mungu wetu amemtia mikononi mwetu \q Samsoni adui yetu."
sw.R: Watawala wa Wafilisti walikusanyika kwa sikukuu kubwa. Walimtolea mungu wao Dagoni dhabihu, wakasherehekea. \q Walisema, "Mungu wetu ametukabidhi Samsoni, \q Samsoni adui yetu!"

es.L: Y los jefes de los filisteos se reunieron para ofrecer un gran sacrificio a Dagón su dios y para regocijarse, \q y dijeron: «Nuestro dios ha entregado en nuestra mano \q a Sansón nuestro enemigo».
es.B: Los jefes de los filisteos se reunieron para ofrecer un gran sacrificio a su dios Dagón y para celebrar. \q Decían: «Nuestro dios ha entregado en nuestras manos \q a Sansón, nuestro enemigo».
es.R: Los jefes filisteos se reunieron para una gran fiesta. Ofrecieron sacrificios a su dios Dagón y celebraron. \q Decían: «Nuestro dios nos ha entregado a Sansón, \q ¡a Sansón, nuestro enemigo!».

decisions.choice: Dagon their god
decisions.reason: Dagon was a chief god of the Philistines, with temples at Gaza and Ashdod (1 Samuel 5:1-7). He was worshiped across the region long before the Philistines came. His name is probably linked to the word for grain, and he was likely a god of crops; the old idea that he was a fish-god rests only on the sound of the Hebrew word for fish and is doubtful.

decisions.choice: Our god has given Samson into our hand
decisions.reason: The Philistines thank Dagon. The reader knows better: Samson fell because the LORD had left him (verse 20), and the LORD will answer his prayer (verses 28-30). The scene becomes a contest between the LORD and Dagon, as again in 1 Samuel 5.

decisions.choice: a chant: a short victory song
decisions.reason: Their words are a chant. In Hebrew the lines end in the same sound, "-enu" ("our"), again and again in verse 24, the kind of verse a crowd would shout together.

decisions.choice: a great festival ... offered sacrifices
decisions.reason: Readable says the "great sacrifice" was a religious feast with offerings.

decisions.choice: the chant of verses 23-24 set in lines
decisions.reason: The Philistines' victory chant (m3) is set as poetry. The lines break where the Hebrew accents divide each verse, at the point where the narrator's words give way to the chant, and between the chant's short rhyming phrases.

decisions.choice: "Dagoni" for Dagon; the god is "mungu wao" with a small m
decisions.reason: Swahili writes "Mungu" with a capital for God and "mungu" with a small letter for the god of another people, as English does with "God" and "god"; the chant of verses 23-24 keeps "mungu wetu" lowercase in the Philistines' mouths.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ הָעָ֔ם וַֽיְהַלְל֖וּ אֶת־אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם כִּ֣י אָמְר֗וּ נָתַ֨ן אֱלֹהֵ֤ינוּ בְיָדֵ֨נוּ֙ אֶת־א֣וֹיְבֵ֔נוּ וְאֵת֙ מַחֲרִ֣יב אַרְצֵ֔נוּ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הִרְבָּ֖ה אֶת־חֲלָלֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw him the people and they praised their god, for they said, has given our god into our hand our enemy and [the] ravager of our land and who multiplied our slain.

en.L: And the people saw him, and they praised their god, \q for they said, "Our god has given into our hand our enemy, \q and the one who laid waste our land, \q and who multiplied our slain."
en.B: When the people saw him, they praised their god. \q They said, "Our god has given into our hands our enemy, \q the one who laid waste our land \q and killed so many of us."
en.R: When the people saw Samson, they praised their god. \q They said, "Our god has handed over to us our enemy, \q the one who ruined our land \q and killed so many of our people!"

sw.L: Nao watu walipomwona, wakamsifu mungu wao, \q kwa maana walisema, "Mungu wetu amemtia mkononi mwetu adui yetu, \q naye aliyeiharibu nchi yetu, \q aliyewaongeza waliouawa kwetu."
sw.B: Watu walipomwona, walimsifu mungu wao. \q Walisema, "Mungu wetu amemtia mikononi mwetu adui yetu, \q yule aliyeiharibu nchi yetu \q na kuwaua wengi wetu."
sw.R: Watu walipomwona Samsoni, walimsifu mungu wao. \q Walisema, "Mungu wetu ametukabidhi adui yetu, \q yule aliyeiharibu nchi yetu \q na kuwaua watu wetu wengi!"

es.L: Y el pueblo lo vio, y alabaron a su dios, \q porque decían: «Nuestro dios ha entregado en nuestra mano a nuestro enemigo, \q y al que asolaba nuestra tierra, \q y al que multiplicaba nuestros muertos».
es.B: Cuando el pueblo lo vio, alabaron a su dios. \q Decían: «Nuestro dios ha entregado en nuestras manos a nuestro enemigo, \q al que asolaba nuestra tierra \q y mataba a tantos de los nuestros».
es.R: Cuando la gente vio a Sansón, alabó a su dios. \q Decían: «Nuestro dios nos ha entregado a nuestro enemigo, \q al que arruinó nuestra tierra \q ¡y mató a tantos de los nuestros!».

decisions.choice: the people saw him
decisions.reason: Samson is brought out only in verse 25, so the story may be telling the crowd's praise ahead of the scene, or the people saw him as he was led in. Either way, the sight of the blind prisoner set them praising Dagon.

decisions.choice: the ravager of our land, who multiplied our slain
decisions.reason: They remember what he did to them: the grain fields, vineyards and olive groves he burned (15:4-5), and the men he killed (14:19; 15:8, 15).

decisions.choice: the chant goes on
decisions.reason: As in verse 23, the lines rhyme in Hebrew on "our": our hand, our enemy, our land, our slain.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּט֣וֹב לִבָּ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ קִרְא֥וּ לְשִׁמְשׁ֖וֹן וִישַֽׂחֶק־לָ֑נוּ וַיִּקְרְא֨וּ לְשִׁמְשׁ֜וֹן מִבֵּ֣ית הָאֲסוּרִ֗ים וַיְצַחֵק֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּעֲמִ֥ידוּ אוֹת֖וֹ בֵּ֥ין הָעַמּוּדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was when [was] good their heart, and they said, call for Samson, and let him make sport for us. And they called for Samson from [the] house of the prisoners, and he made sport before them, and they made stand him between the pillars.

en.L: And it came about, when their hearts were merry, that they said, "Call Samson, that he may entertain us." And they called Samson from the house of the prisoners, and he performed before them; and they made him stand between the pillars.
en.B: When they were in high spirits, they said, "Call for Samson, and let him entertain us." So they called Samson out of the prison, and he performed for them. They had him stand between the pillars.
en.R: The people were having a good time. They said, "Bring Samson out here. Let him do something to make us laugh." So they brought Samson out of the prison, and he entertained them. They made him stand between the pillars of the temple.

sw.L: Ikawa mioyo yao ilipokuwa na furaha, wakasema, "Mwiteni Samsoni, atuchezee." Nao wakamwita Samsoni kutoka nyumba ya wafungwa, naye akacheza mbele yao; wakamsimamisha kati ya nguzo.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wamechangamka, walisema, "Mwiteni Samsoni atuburudishe." Basi walimwita Samsoni kutoka gerezani, naye akawachezea. Walimsimamisha kati ya nguzo.
sw.R: Watu walikuwa wakifurahi. Walisema, "Mleteni Samsoni hapa. Afanye jambo la kutuchekesha." Kwa hiyo walimleta Samsoni kutoka gerezani, naye akawaburudisha. Walimsimamisha kati ya nguzo za hekalu.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando su corazón estaba alegre, dijeron: «{{plural_you:Llamen|Llamad}} a Sansón, para que nos divierta». Y llamaron a Sansón de la casa de los presos, y él hizo de bufón delante de ellos; y lo pusieron en pie entre las columnas.
es.B: Cuando ya estaban muy alegres, dijeron: «{{plural_you:Llamen|Llamad}} a Sansón para que nos divierta». Así que sacaron a Sansón de la cárcel, y él los divirtió. Lo pusieron de pie entre las columnas.
es.R: La gente se estaba divirtiendo mucho. Dijeron: «{{plural_you:Traigan|Traed}} aquí a Sansón. Que haga algo para hacernos reír». Así que sacaron a Sansón de la cárcel, y él los entretuvo. Lo pusieron de pie entre las columnas del templo.

decisions.choice: when their hearts were merry: in high spirits
decisions.reason: "A good heart" here means cheerful, often from wine at a feast (1 Samuel 25:36; Esther 1:10).

decisions.choice: let him entertain us
alternatives: let him make sport for us
decisions.reason: The two verbs used here come from the word for laughing. He was made to perform: perhaps feats of strength, perhaps simply to be laughed at as a blind fool. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: when their hearts were merry
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "for [it was] good", and the reading marked in the margin has "when [it was] good". The difference is one letter and the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the pillars of the temple
decisions.reason: Readable says that "the house" where this happens is Dagon's temple (verses 26-27).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שִׁמְשׁ֜וֹן אֶל־הַנַּ֨עַר הַמַּחֲזִ֣יק בְּיָדוֹ֮ הַנִּ֣יחָה אוֹתִי֒ וַהֲמִשֵׁ֨נִי֙ אֶת־הָֽעַמֻּדִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הַבַּ֖יִת נָכ֣וֹן עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֶשָּׁעֵ֖ן עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Samson to the young man holding his hand, let me rest and let me feel the pillars which the house [is] set on them, and I will lean on them.

en.L: And Samson said to the young man who held him by his hand, "Let me rest, and let me feel the pillars on which the house is set, so that I may lean on them."
en.B: Samson said to the young man who was leading him by the hand, "Let me rest here and feel the pillars that hold up the temple, so that I can lean against them."
en.R: A young servant was holding Samson's hand to lead him. Samson said to him, "Let me feel the pillars that hold up the temple. I want to lean against them and rest."

sw.L: Naye Samsoni akamwambia yule kijana aliyemshika mkono, "Niache nipumzike, nizipapase nguzo ambazo nyumba imesimama juu yake, ili niziegemee."
sw.B: Samsoni alimwambia yule kijana aliyekuwa akimwongoza kwa mkono, "Niache nipumzike hapa na kuzipapasa nguzo zinazolishikilia hekalu, ili niziegemee."
sw.R: Kijana mmoja mtumishi alikuwa amemshika Samsoni mkono kumwongoza. Samsoni alimwambia, "Niache nizipapase nguzo zinazolishikilia hekalu. Nataka kuziegemea na kupumzika."

es.L: Y Sansón dijo al muchacho que lo sostenía de la mano: «Déjame descansar, y déjame tocar las columnas sobre las que está asentada la casa, para que me apoye en ellas».
es.B: Sansón le dijo al muchacho que lo llevaba de la mano: «Déjame descansar aquí y tocar las columnas que sostienen el templo, para apoyarme en ellas».
es.R: Un joven sirviente llevaba a Sansón de la mano. Sansón le dijo: «Déjame tocar las columnas que sostienen el templo. Quiero apoyarme en ellas y descansar».

decisions.choice: the young man: a boy or servant
decisions.reason: The word (na'ar) can mean a boy, a young man, or a servant. Here he is the one guiding the blind prisoner.

decisions.choice: let me rest
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "let me be, leave me" or "let me rest, set me down". Samson asks to stop where he can lean, as a tired prisoner might.

decisions.choice: the pillars on which the house is set
decisions.reason: "The house" is Dagon's temple. Remains of Philistine temples from this time show a roof held up by wooden pillars set on stone bases close together in the middle of the hall. Pull those away, and the roof comes down.

decisions.choice: the temple
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "house", the Hebrew word for a god's house as for any building; Balanced and Readable say "temple".

source.text: וְהַבַּ֗יִת מָלֵ֤א הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ וְהַנָּשִׁ֔ים וְשָׁ֕מָּה כֹּ֖ל סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וְעַל־הַגָּ֗ג כִּשְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֔ה הָרֹאִ֖ים בִּשְׂח֥וֹק שִׁמְשֽׁוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And the house [was] full [of] the men and the women, and there [were] all [the] rulers of [the] Philistines, and on the roof about three thousand man and woman, the [ones] looking at [the] performing of Samson.

en.L: Now the house was full of men and women, and all the rulers of the Philistines [were] there, and on the roof [were] about 3,000 men and women, watching while Samson performed.
en.B: The temple was full of men and women, and all the rulers of the Philistines were there. On the roof there were about 3,000 men and women looking on as Samson performed.
en.R: The temple was crowded with men and women. All the Philistine rulers were there. About 3,000 more men and women were up on the roof. They were all watching Samson entertain them.

sw.L: Na nyumba ilikuwa imejaa wanaume na wanawake, na watawala wote wa Wafilisti [walikuwa] huko, na juu ya dari [walikuwa] wanaume na wanawake kama 3,000, wakitazama Samsoni alipokuwa akicheza.
sw.B: Hekalu lilikuwa limejaa wanaume na wanawake, na watawala wote wa Wafilisti walikuwa humo. Juu ya dari palikuwa na wanaume na wanawake kama 3,000 wakitazama Samsoni alipokuwa akicheza.
sw.R: Hekalu lilikuwa limejaa wanaume na wanawake. Watawala wote wa Wafilisti walikuwa humo. Wanaume na wanawake wengine kama 3,000 walikuwa juu ya dari. Wote walikuwa wakimtazama Samsoni akiwaburudisha.

es.L: Y la casa estaba llena de hombres y mujeres, y todos los jefes de los filisteos [estaban] allí, y sobre el techo [había] como 3000 hombres y mujeres, que miraban mientras Sansón hacía de bufón.
es.B: El templo estaba lleno de hombres y mujeres, y todos los jefes de los filisteos estaban allí. En la azotea había unos 3000 hombres y mujeres que miraban a Sansón mientras los divertía.
es.R: El templo estaba repleto de hombres y mujeres. Todos los jefes filisteos estaban allí. Arriba, en la azotea, había unos 3000 hombres y mujeres más. Todos miraban cómo Sansón los entretenía.

decisions.choice: about 3,000 on the roof
decisions.reason: Roofs were flat and could hold a crowd. The people on the roof watched Samson below, which tells how great the fall of the building would be.

decisions.choice: all the rulers of the Philistines
decisions.reason: All five rulers who had bought Samson's betrayal are present, which sets up the end in verse 30.

decisions.choice: the temple
decisions.reason: As in verse 26.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א שִׁמְשׁ֛וֹן אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יֱהֹוִ֡ה זָכְרֵ֣נִי נָא֩ וְחַזְּקֵ֨נִי נָ֜א אַ֣ךְ הַפַּ֤עַם הַזֶּה֙ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְאִנָּקְמָ֧ה נְקַם־אַחַ֛ת מִשְּׁתֵ֥י עֵינַ֖י מִפְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Samson to YHWH and said, my Lord YHWH, remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, only this time, the God, and I will avenge myself [with] vengeance of one for my two eyes from [the] Philistines.

en.L: And Samson called to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, only this once, O God, so that I may avenge myself on the Philistines with one vengeance for my two eyes."
en.B: Then Samson called out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, please remember me. Please give me strength just this once more, O God, so that with one blow I may pay the Philistines back for my two eyes."
en.R: Then Samson prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, please remember me. God, please make me strong just one more time. Then I can pay back the Philistines for my two eyes, all at one time."
