sw.L: Naye Samsoni akamwita {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akasema, "Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, unikumbuke, tafadhali, unitie nguvu, tafadhali, mara hii moja tu, Ee Mungu, ili nijilipizie kisasi kwa Wafilisti kisasi kimoja kwa ajili ya macho yangu mawili."
sw.B: Kisha Samsoni alimlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: "Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, tafadhali unikumbuke. Tafadhali unipe nguvu mara hii moja tu tena, Ee Mungu, ili kwa pigo moja niwalipize Wafilisti kwa ajili ya macho yangu mawili."
sw.R: Kisha Samsoni alimwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Alisema, "Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, tafadhali unikumbuke. Mungu, tafadhali nipe nguvu mara moja tu tena. Ndipo nitaweza kuwalipiza Wafilisti kwa ajili ya macho yangu mawili, wote kwa mara moja."

es.L: Y Sansón clamó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y dijo: «Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, acuérdate de mí, te ruego, y fortaléceme, te ruego, solamente esta vez, oh Dios, para que me vengue de los filisteos con una sola venganza por mis dos ojos».
es.B: Entonces Sansón clamó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, por favor, acuérdate de mí. Por favor, dame fuerzas solo una vez más, oh Dios, para que de un solo golpe me vengue de los filisteos por mis dos ojos».
es.R: Entonces Sansón oró {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Le dijo: «Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, por favor, acuérdate de mí. Dios, por favor, hazme fuerte solo una vez más. Así podré vengarme de los filisteos por mis dos ojos, todo de una vez».

decisions.choice: the LORD; Lord GOD; God
decisions.reason: Samson calls on the LORD by his name (YHWH), as "my Lord YHWH" (Adonai YHWH), and as God (ha-elohim). Where the name follows "Lord" it is read aloud as "God", so the two words are not both read as "Lord".

decisions.choice: remember me
decisions.reason: In prayer, "remember" means more than recall: it asks God to act for someone (Genesis 8:1; 30:22; 1 Samuel 1:19). It is Samson's first prayer since his thirst at Lehi (15:18).

decisions.choice: one act of vengeance for my two eyes
alternatives: vengeance for one of my two eyes
decisions.reason: The words can be read as "one vengeance for my two eyes", a single blow to repay both, or as "vengeance for one of my two eyes", as if all he could do would not repay both. The first is followed here.

decisions.choice: Samson prays for revenge
decisions.reason: He asks to pay back what was done to him. The narrator neither praises nor blames the request; the LORD answers it, and through it Samson does what he was born for, to begin to save Israel from the Philistines (13:5).

decisions.choice: prayed to
decisions.reason: Calling to the LORD here is prayer, so Readable says "prayed".

decisions.choice: "Bwana MUNGU" for Lord GOD (Adonai YHWH), the divine name in capitals inside the setting span
decisions.reason: As in the Pentateuch drafts: Adonai stays "Bwana", and the name that follows is "MUNGU" in capitals so that it is not written "Bwana BWANA"; the reader setting gives "Bwana Yahwe".

decisions.choice: "Señor DIOS" by default, "Señor Yahvé" with the divine name setting
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch terms set for Adonai YHWH: "Señor" for the Hebrew "Lord" and "DIOS" in capitals for the divine name, which the setting turns into "Yahvé", like the English "Lord GOD" / "Lord Yahweh".

source.text: וַיִּלְפֹּ֨ת שִׁמְשׁ֜וֹן אֶת־שְׁנֵ֣י׀עַמּוּדֵ֣י הַתָּ֗וֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הַבַּ֨יִת֙ נָכ֣וֹן עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּסָּמֵ֖ךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם אֶחָ֥ד בִּימִינ֖וֹ וְאֶחָ֥ד בִּשְׂמֹאלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And grasped Samson [the] two pillars of the middle which the house [was] set on them, and he leaned on them, one in his right and one in his left.

en.L: And Samson grasped the two middle pillars on which the house was set, and he braced himself against them, one with his right [hand] and one with his left.
en.B: Samson took hold of the two middle pillars on which the temple stood, and he braced himself against them, his right hand on one and his left hand on the other.
en.R: Samson reached out and found the two pillars in the middle of the temple. They held up the whole building. He set his right hand against one pillar and his left against the other, and he leaned on them with all his weight.

sw.L: Naye Samsoni akazishika zile nguzo mbili za katikati ambazo nyumba ilikuwa imesimama juu yake, akajiegemeza juu yake, moja kwa [mkono] wake wa kuume na moja kwa wa kushoto.
sw.B: Samsoni alizishika zile nguzo mbili za katikati ambazo hekalu lilikuwa limesimama juu yake, akajiegemeza juu yake, mkono wake wa kuume kwenye moja na mkono wa kushoto kwenye nyingine.
sw.R: Samsoni alinyosha mikono, akazipata zile nguzo mbili zilizokuwa katikati ya hekalu. Ndizo zilizolishikilia jengo lote. Aliweka mkono wake wa kuume kwenye nguzo moja na wa kushoto kwenye nyingine, akaziegemea kwa uzito wake wote.

es.L: Y Sansón asió las dos columnas del medio sobre las que estaba asentada la casa, y se apoyó contra ellas, una con su [mano] derecha y otra con su izquierda.
es.B: Sansón se aferró a las dos columnas centrales sobre las que se sostenía el templo, y se apoyó contra ellas, con la mano derecha en una y la izquierda en la otra.
es.R: Sansón extendió los brazos y encontró las dos columnas del centro del templo. Ellas sostenían todo el edificio. Puso la mano derecha contra una columna y la izquierda contra la otra, y se apoyó en ellas con todo su peso.

decisions.choice: grasped: took firm hold
decisions.reason: The verb means to clasp or to twist; in Ruth 3:8 it is used of turning over. Here Samson wraps his hands around the pillars.

decisions.choice: one with his right and one with his left
decisions.reason: "Hand" is understood: one pillar under each hand.

decisions.choice: [hand] (L); hand (B, R); They held up the whole building (R)
decisions.reason: The word the Hebrew leaves understood is supplied (m2). Readable also says why these pillars mattered (verse 26).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שִׁמְשׁ֗וֹן תָּמ֣וֹת נַפְשִׁי֮ עִם־פְּלִשְׁתִּים֒ וַיֵּ֣ט בְּכֹ֔חַ וַיִּפֹּ֤ל הַבַּ֨יִת֙ עַל־הַסְּרָנִ֔ים וְעַל־כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־בּ֑וֹ וַיִּהְי֤וּ הַמֵּתִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵמִ֣ית בְּמוֹת֔וֹ רַבִּ֕ים מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵמִ֖ית בְּחַיָּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Samson, let die my soul with [the] Philistines. And he stretched out with strength, and fell the house on the rulers and on all the people that [was] in it. And were the dead whom he killed in his death many more than whom he had killed in his life.

en.L: And Samson said, "Let my soul die with the Philistines!" And he stretched out with [all his] strength, and the house fell on the rulers and on all the people who [were] in it. And the dead whom he killed at his death were more than those whom he had killed in his life.
en.B: And Samson said, "Let me die together with the Philistines!" He pushed with all his might, and down came the temple on the rulers and on all the people inside. So he killed more people by his death than he had killed during his whole life.
en.R: Samson said, "Let me die together with the Philistines!" Then he pushed as hard as he could. The temple fell down on the rulers and on everyone in it. Samson killed more people when he died than he had killed while he was alive.

sw.L: Naye Samsoni akasema, "Roho yangu na ife pamoja na Wafilisti!" Naye akajinyoosha kwa nguvu [zake zote], nayo nyumba ikawaangukia watawala na watu wote [waliokuwa] ndani yake. Nao wafu aliowaua katika kufa kwake walikuwa wengi kuliko wale aliowaua katika maisha yake.
sw.B: Samsoni alisema, "Na nife pamoja na Wafilisti!" Akasukuma kwa nguvu zake zote, na hekalu likawaangukia watawala na watu wote waliokuwa ndani. Hivyo aliwaua watu wengi zaidi katika kufa kwake kuliko aliowaua katika maisha yake yote.
sw.R: Samsoni alisema, "Na nife pamoja na Wafilisti!" Kisha akasukuma kwa nguvu zake zote. Hekalu likawaangukia watawala na kila mtu aliyekuwa ndani yake. Samsoni aliwaua watu wengi zaidi alipokufa kuliko aliowaua alipokuwa hai.

es.L: Y dijo Sansón: «¡Muera mi alma con los filisteos!». Y empujó con [toda su] fuerza, y la casa cayó sobre los jefes y sobre todo el pueblo que [estaba] en ella. Y los muertos que mató al morir fueron más que los que había matado en su vida.
es.B: Y Sansón dijo: «¡Que muera yo junto con los filisteos!». Empujó con todas sus fuerzas, y el templo se vino abajo sobre los jefes y sobre toda la gente que estaba dentro. Así mató a más gente con su muerte que en toda su vida.
es.R: Sansón dijo: «¡Que muera yo junto con los filisteos!». Entonces empujó con todas sus fuerzas. El templo se derrumbó sobre los jefes y sobre todos los que estaban adentro. Sansón mató a más gente al morir que en toda su vida.

decisions.choice: let my soul die: let me die
decisions.reason: The soul (nefesh) here is the person's life or self; "let my soul die" means simply "let me die".

decisions.choice: Samson's death with the Philistines
decisions.reason: Samson does not die in despair; he dies doing what he was born for, striking the Philistines (13:5). He is later named among those who acted by faith (Hebrews 11:32).

decisions.choice: he stretched out with strength: he pushed hard
decisions.reason: The verb means to stretch out or bend. He threw all his strength against the two pillars.

decisions.choice: he killed more people by his death than during his life
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make Samson the subject of the closing sentence, which says the same thing more simply than "the dead whom he killed ... were more".

source.text: וַיֵּרְד֨וּ אֶחָ֜יו וְכָל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִיהוּ֮ וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ אֹתוֹ֒ וַֽיַּעֲל֣וּ׀וַיִּקְבְּר֣וּ אוֹת֗וֹ בֵּ֤ין צָרְעָה֙ וּבֵ֣ין אֶשְׁתָּאֹ֔ל בְּקֶ֖בֶר מָנ֣וֹחַ אָבִ֑יו וְה֛וּא שָׁפַ֥ט אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And went down his brothers and all [the] house of his father and lifted him, and they brought up and buried him between Zorah and between Eshtaol in [the] tomb of Manoah his father. And he had judged Israel twenty year[s].

en.L: And his brothers and all the house of his father came down and took him, and they brought [him] up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. And he had judged Israel twenty years.
en.B: Then his brothers and all his father's family came down. They took him and brought him back up, and they buried him in the tomb of Manoah his father, between Zorah and Eshtaol. He had judged Israel for twenty years.
en.R: Then Samson's brothers and his father's whole family came down to Gaza. They took his body and carried it back home. They buried him in his father Manoah's tomb, between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson had led Israel for twenty years.

sw.L: Nao ndugu zake na nyumba yote ya baba yake wakashuka, wakamchukua, wakampandisha, wakamzika kati ya Sora na Eshtaoli katika kaburi la Manoa baba yake. Naye alikuwa amewaamua Israeli miaka ishirini.
sw.B: Kisha ndugu zake na jamaa yote ya baba yake walishuka. Walimchukua, wakampandisha, wakamzika katika kaburi la Manoa baba yake, kati ya Sora na Eshtaoli. Alikuwa amewaamua Israeli kwa miaka ishirini.
sw.R: Kisha ndugu zake Samsoni na jamaa yote ya baba yake walishuka Gaza. Walichukua mwili wake, wakaurudisha nyumbani. Walimzika katika kaburi la baba yake Manoa, kati ya Sora na Eshtaoli. Samsoni alikuwa amewaongoza Israeli kwa miaka ishirini.

es.L: Y descendieron sus hermanos y toda la casa de su padre y lo tomaron, y [lo] subieron y lo sepultaron entre Zora y Estaol, en el sepulcro de Manoa su padre. Y él había juzgado a Israel veinte años.
es.B: Después sus hermanos y toda la familia de su padre bajaron a buscarlo. Se lo llevaron de vuelta y lo sepultaron en el sepulcro de su padre Manoa, entre Zora y Estaol. Había juzgado a Israel durante veinte años.
es.R: Después los hermanos de Sansón y toda la familia de su padre bajaron a Gaza. Tomaron su cuerpo y lo llevaron de vuelta a casa. Lo sepultaron en la tumba de su padre Manoa, entre Zora y Estaol. Sansón había dirigido a Israel durante veinte años.

decisions.choice: buried between Zorah and Eshtaol in Manoah's tomb
decisions.reason: His story ends where it began: the Spirit of the LORD first stirred him "between Zorah and Eshtaol" (13:25). Burial in the family tomb mattered greatly; the man who lived among foreigners is laid with his father.

decisions.choice: his brothers
decisions.reason: Samson was his mother's first child (13:2-3). "Brothers" may be younger brothers born later, or close relatives, as the word often means.

decisions.choice: he had judged Israel twenty years
decisions.reason: As at 2:16, a judge was a leader raised up to rescue and govern Israel. The same total closes the account of his deeds in 15:20, "in the days of the Philistines"; here it ends his life. The Philistines still ruled Israel when he died (13:1, 5).

decisions.choice: to Gaza; his body; back home; led Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says where they went and what they carried, and uses "led" for "judged" as at 2:16. Balanced supplies "him" for the object Literal brackets.
